interpro/panther/PTHR32294/PTHR32294-rev.preferred_name: Type-C (DnaE/PolC) DNA polymerase alpha subunits, replicative and error-prone
interpro/panther/PTHR32294/PTHR32294-rev.summary: Bacterial C-family DNA polymerases share templated DNA-synthesis chemistry but differ in replication role and proofreading architecture. SF0 includes replicative DnaE1 and Bacillus DnaE3: E. coli and Pseudomonas implementations use a separate DnaQ exonuclease, whereas M. tuberculosis DnaE1 has an experimentally active intrinsic PHP domain. Bacillus DnaE3 extends RNA primers before handoff to PolC and can be proofread by PolC. SF5 PolC contains an intrinsic DnaQ-like proofreading domain. SF4 DnaE2 proteins supply damage-tolerant synthesis and do not substitute for the ordinary replicative polymerase. Broad family or subfamily membership alone does not establish a native polymerase role or an active PHP proofreader.
interpro/panther/PTHR32294/PTHR32294-rev.coherence_reason: DNA-directed DNA polymerase chemistry is the shared property assessed by the existing PAINT root judgment. Chromosome-replication role and intrinsic proofreading require finer distinctions, including distinctions within SF0. Being partnered with DnaQ is not intrinsic exonuclease activity of the alpha subunit.

interpro/panther/PTHR33516/PTHR33516-rev.preferred_name: LexA-family SOS repressors and related S24 peptidase autoprotease repressors
interpro/panther/PTHR33516/PTHR33516-rev.summary: The LexA repressors and their structural relatives: winged-helix DNA-binding proteins fused to a peptidase S24 autoprotease domain. A member binds a palindromic operator and represses transcription; when RecA is activated on damage-generated single-stranded DNA it stimulates the repressor's autocatalytic cleavage at an Ala-Gly bond, which separates the DNA-binding domain from the dimerization domain and derepresses the regulon. The family contains both the principal SOS repressors and lineage-specific paralogs with narrow regulons, as well as phage repressors of the same architecture, which PANTHER keeps in the single subfamily SF2 alongside the bacterial proteins.
interpro/panther/PTHR33516/PTHR33516-rev.coherence_reason: Operator binding, transcriptional repression and RecA-stimulated autocleavage are shared across the family and are what the PAINT node asserts. What differs is which genes a member represses: the principal LexA of a genome controls the SOS regulon, whereas paralogs can control as little as their own operon, and the phage repressors in the same subfamily maintain lysogeny rather than participating in the host SOS response. Regulon-specific process claims therefore do not transfer between members, even though the molecular functions do.

The subfamily therefore cannot be used to distinguish a principal SOS repressor from a narrow-regulon paralog or from a prophage maintenance repressor.

Two of the family's five PAINT assertions are the interesting ones. The four that concern binding and repression are sound at the bacterial LexA node because they say nothing about the regulon. The SOS response assertion is left UNRESOLVED: it is right for a genome's principal LexA and wrong for a narrow-regulon paralog such as LexA2, and nothing available here says how many clade members are of each kind. That is also why the module keeps its LexA part optional and species-neutral: which paralog gates the imuA-imuB-dnaE2 cassette varies between genomes. interpro/panther/PTHR35369/PTHR35369-rev.preferred_name: SulA cell-division inhibitors and the ImuA/ImuB accessory proteins of damage-induced mutagenesis
interpro/panther/PTHR35369/PTHR35369-rev.summary: A small bacterial family that PANTHER keeps together on sequence similarity but which contains two functionally unrelated kinds of SOS protein. SF4 holds the SulA cell-division inhibitors, which bind FtsZ and block Z-ring assembly after DNA damage. SF2 holds the ImuB proteins: UmuC/Y-family folds that have lost the catalytic carboxylates and act as the adaptor of the ImuA-ImuB-DnaE2 damage-induced mutagenesis cassette, binding ImuA, the DnaE2 polymerase and the beta clamp. SF3 holds the proteobacterial ImuA accessory proteins of the same cassette, which share weak similarity with SulA and RecA. Nothing in the family is a DNA polymerase and nothing in it repairs DNA: SF4 delays division, SF2 and SF3 hand damaged templates to a polymerase encoded elsewhere.
interpro/panther/PTHR35369/PTHR35369-rev.coherence_reason: Membership of the SOS response is all the subfamilies share. SF4 inhibits cell division through FtsZ binding; SF2 and SF3 are accessory components of translesion synthesis and have no effect on division. Neither molecular function nor biological process transfers across that boundary, and the family name, taken from an uncharacterized Bradyrhizobium protein, describes neither group.

interpro/panther/PTHR35369/PTHR35369-rev.notes:
Written while promoting modules/bacterial_imuabc_damage_induced_mutagenesis.yaml to COMPLETE, which grounds its ImuA and ImuB steps here. Three points worth carrying forward. First, the family term is far too broad to be the module's descriptor, so the module grounds the ImuA role on InterPro families and the ImuB role on the Pfam IMS domain, and points here for the subfamily split. Second, the SulA-derived cell-division term that reaches ImuA proteins is not an absent-signature artifact: IPR004596 genuinely matches the ImuA clade, because ImuA and SulA are homologous, and it carries GO:0051782 and GO:0009432 in InterPro2GO. The family entry IPR050356, which covers this whole PANTHER family, carries no GO mapping at all. The removal in the member review therefore rests on biology, not on the signature set.
Third, the ImuA proteins are split across two InterPro families that do not correspond to one PANTHER subfamily: P. putida ImuA (Q88I84) carries IPR047610 and sits in SF3, while Caulobacter ImuA (Q9A3J1) carries IPR017026 and has no PANTHER assignment at all, so SF3 cannot be used as the module's selector for the ImuA role. Fourth, the actinobacterial counterpart ImuA' (M. tuberculosis Rv3395c, P9WKZ9) has a distinct sequence/domain classification and is modeled as another family realization of the accessory step, not as a member of this family. No unified family assignment is established here; distinct sequence classifications do not exclude homology of RecA-like structural components. Node depth for PTN002176549 was read from the PANTHER 19 treeinfo service (pantherdb.org/services/oai/pantherdb/treeinfo?family=PTHR35369).

interpro/panther/PTHR45900/PTHR45900-rev.preferred_name: RecA-related recombinases and ImuA accessory proteins
interpro/panther/PTHR45900/PTHR45900-rev.summary: Canonical bacterial RecA proteins and plant organellar RecA homologs bind single-stranded DNA, form nucleoprotein filaments and catalyze ATP-dependent strand exchange. Activated bacterial RecA can also stimulate LexA repressor autocleavage. These functions describe well-characterized RecA members, not every protein assigned to this family. Current UniProt classification places the experimentally identified Myxococcus xanthus ImuA (Q1D5A2/MXAN_3991) in PTHR45900:SF1. node_assessments.assessment_reason: The seed is E. coli RecA, which really is a component of the Pol V mutasome: the active complex is UmuD'2C-RecA-ATP. But the term names a specific complex built from the umuDC gene products, and it has been placed at the family root (LUCA), so every RecA homolog inherits membership of an enterobacterial translesion-synthesis complex. The over-reach is checkable in GOA: Arabidopsis RECA2 (Q8RY99) and RECA3 (Q9ZUP2), both mitochondrially targeted plant proteins, carry GO:0009355 IBA from this node and this seed, and so does M. tuberculosis RecA (P9WHJ3), whose genome has no umuDC at all. Mycobacteria instead use the ImuA'-ImuB-DnaE2 cassette, described in the literature as the non-orthologous replacement of the umuDC system, so the inherited complex does not exist in that lineage. The term belongs on the enterobacterial RecA clade at most, and arguably only on members shown to participate in a Pol V complex.

interpro/panther/PTHR45900/PTHR45900-rev.notes: Written while promoting modules/bacterial_imuabc_damage_induced_mutagenesis.yaml to COMPLETE, whose optional RecA signalling step is grounded here through P. putida RecA. Three of the five root-placed PAINT assertions are sound (ssDNA binding, strand exchange, recombinational repair); two over-reach, and both are reported for upstream attention. GO:0009355 (DNA polymerase V complex) propagates an enterobacterial complex to plant organellar homologs and to mycobacterial RecA, whose lineage replaced umuDC with the very cassette this module describes. GO:0004520 (DNA endonuclease activity) propagates the activity of the PI-MtuI intein carried by the M. tuberculosis recA allele, which was assayed on the excised intervening sequence (PMID:11850426) rather than on RecA; the intein evidence is cited from that cached publication rather than from the UniProt flat file, since there is no local genes/MYCTU/recA folder against which a flat-file quote could be checked. Neither affects the module's own exemplar: Q88ME4 carries no IBA rows at all. Node depth was read from the PANTHER 19 treeinfo service (pantherdb.org/services/oai/pantherdb/treeinfo?family=PTHR45900), which reports PTN000534381 as the ROOT node with taxonomic range LUCA. The subfamily labels are PANTHER's official names, verbatim, and are misleading for SF1: those 670 members are bacterial RecA proteins, not mitochondrial. Follow-up: primary-source sequence mapping identifies MXAN_3991/Q1D5A2 as M. xanthus ImuA. The reviewed-only inventory did not include this unreviewed UniProt entry. Current classification includes it in SF1, but its leaf is absent from the cached PAINT tree. Universal mechanistic prose and the family-wide sensor scope have therefore been narrowed without changing any existing node identifiers, seeds, verdicts or raw PAINT rows. The subsequent Figure 4E reinspection supports an assay-scoped ImuA strand-exchange exception, without asserting a loss event or LexA co-protease activity. A native recombinational-repair process exception remains unestablished. No HMM classification defect is inferred from the automated RecName. The 2021 publication cache remains abstract-only; externally read full text and the Figure 1 identity proof are documented in the linked consultation. The 2024 full text supports positive DNA binding and ATP hydrolysis, not universal RecA chemistry.
